solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Muscle ailing during army corps dance

parts.note: quad is short for quadriceps, the big thigh muscle

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another, so ill goes within the corps

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A sick muscle strikes while the army engineers hold a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrille is a square dance for four couples, popular in nineteenth-century ballrooms.

clue.text: Pound calamari, removing head

indicators.note: removing the head means the opening letter of squid is taken off

parts.note: calamari is squid served as food

explanation.surface: A cook prices calamari by the pound after cutting off the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is the informal British word for one pound sterling in money.

clue.text: Jack and Mark do not vote

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Two people called Jack and Mark refuse to cast their ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to deliberately decline to cast a ballot in an election or motion.

clue.text: Artist capturing island and drowned valley

indicators.note: capturing means holding something within, so the island sits inside the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter depicts an island and a flooded valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley.

clue.text: Small illuminated atelier regularly visited

parts.note: lit means illuminated

indicators.note: regularly visited means only every other letter of atelier is called on

explanation.surface: A small, well-lit artist's studio gets frequent visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly visited' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of atelier, T, L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Little is a plain synonym for small in size.

clue.text: Awaiting or missing cough medicine

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word or is taken out of the medicine

parts.note: an expectorant is a cough medicine that loosens phlegm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone waits for, or goes without, their cough mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link between two definitions, but it is the letters removed from EXPECTORANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being expectant means looking forward to something that is anticipated to happen.

clue.text: British government abroad runs a judiciary initially

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of judiciary is wanted

explanation.surface: A colonial administration overseas operates a court system.
explanation.walkthrough: The Raj was British rule in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was the period of British imperial rule over the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Learn working of the kidneys

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of learn being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A student studies how the kidneys function.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: One's foolish when gripped by cards

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so when sits within the cards

parts.note: jacks are playing cards
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone looks silly when caught holding the wrong cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a stupid person, so the word names someone who is foolish.

clue.text: Tins arranged by worker without delay

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of tins are put in a different order

parts.note: an ant is a worker in crossword convention

explanation.surface: A worker swiftly lines up some tin cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant can mean immediately or at once, happening straight away.

clue.text: Suddenly frighten fryer in charge

parts.note: a frying pan is a fryer

explanation.surface: A cook in charge of the frying pan gets a sudden fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To panic someone is to fill them with sudden alarm or terror.

clue.text: Valerie cops everyone tipping over wine

parts.note: Val is short for Valerie
cops are the police

indicators.note: tipping over means turning upside down, so all is read the other way

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Valerie and the police all knock over a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Valpolicella is a red wine from the Veneto region of northern Italy.

clue.text: Criticise a clerk, we hear, producing cigar

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: we hear means the next word is taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk

explanation.surface: Someone berates an office worker and ends up with a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: TELLER said in a non-rhotic British accent sounds like TELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long, slender type of cigar.

clue.text: Sound of sheep eating grandma's fruit

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so grandma goes into the bleat

parts.note: baa is the bleat of a sheep
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A bleating sheep munches the fruit that belongs to grandma.
explanation.walkthrough: Nan is everyday British English for a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with a yellow skin.

clue.text: Composer somewhere in Germany briefly joins Australian

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of Berlin goes

parts.note: Berlin is the German capital
Oz is an informal name for Australia, standing for Australian

explanation.surface: A composer from a German city teams up with an Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer, known for the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Type of grass father's maintaining foremost in meadow

indicators.note: maintaining means holding up from within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: papa's, a father's, written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: foremost in means the leading letter of meadow

explanation.surface: Dad keeps the best grass in the meadow going.
explanation.definitionFit: Pampas grass is a tall ornamental grass with feathery plumes, native to South America.

clue.text: Argument after work upset new religious leader

indicators.note: after places the argument at the end, following the other pieces
upset means overturned, so the work is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tiff is a small argument

explanation.surface: After a quarrel at work, a new church leader is unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: The pontiff is the Pope, head of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Salt put on waterproof surface of road?

parts.note: a salt and a tar are both old sailors
a mac is a waterproof coat

explanation.surface: Someone puts salt on the road surface to keep it from freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' suggests gritting icy roads, but it is the sailor; a mac is a British raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the asphalt-type material laid on roads, the paving underfoot.

clue.text: Ancient tablet, pink and dry, son ate stupidly

parts.note: rose is a pink colour
TT means teetotal, i.e. dry

indicators.note: stupidly means foolishly mixed up, so son ate is jumbled

explanation.surface: A pink, dry ancient tablet was foolishly eaten by someone's son.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone is an inscribed Egyptian slab that unlocked hieroglyphics.

clue.text: Doze, sheltered in special clothing

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so special encloses the sheltered part

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, as in the lee of a wall

explanation.surface: Someone snoozes, cosy in special nightwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep is to rest with eyes closed, a fuller version of a nap or snooze.

clue.text: Antony cut in half unknown gemstone

indicators.note: cut in half means the front half of the name Antony is chopped away, leaving the back three letters

parts.note: X is the mathematician's unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Antony splits an unidentified gemstone in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Perfect date in Rome, mostly by a lake

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter of Ides is dropped

parts.note: the Ides were dates in the Roman calendar, such as 15 March
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A perfect Roman date takes place beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Huge number working beyond factory unit

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so working is placed last

parts.note: a mill is a factory
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit
on means working, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A vast number of people work past one factory unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A million is a thousand thousands, often used loosely for any enormous quantity.

clue.text: Field northwards contains garland of flowers

indicators.note: northwards in a down clue means reading upwards, from bottom to top
contains means the needed letters are held within the word field

explanation.surface: A field facing north is full of flowers for a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' takes IEL out of Field, and 'northwards' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Tear fastener

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rush along at speed
second meaning: a toothed fastener on clothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' suggests ripping, but here it means to dash along.
explanation.definitionFit: To zip is to move very fast, and a zip is also a sliding clothes fastener.

clue.text: Furry carnivorous mammal biting stump

parts.note: biting cold is arctic cold
to stump someone is to fox, or baffle, them

explanation.surface: A furry meat-eating animal chews on a tree stump.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic fox is a small predatory canine with thick white winter fur.
